name: ws
solves: Provides a fast, lightweight, and RFC-6455 compliant WebSocket client and server implementation for Node.js, handling low-level WebSocket protocol concerns like framing, masking, ping/pong, close handshakes, and permessage-deflate compression.
best_for: Building custom WebSocket servers on Node.js where you need full control over the protocol and connection lifecycle
Adding WebSocket support to an existing Node.js HTTP/HTTPS server (Express, Fastify, etc.) via the upgrade mechanism
High-performance binary data streaming between Node.js services or between server and native clients
Implementing custom real-time protocols where higher-level abstractions like Socket.IO add unnecessary overhead
Microservice-to-microservice low-latency communication over persistent connections
skip_when: You need automatic reconnection, multiplexing, rooms, namespaces, or broadcasting abstractions out of the box — use Socket.IO or a higher-level library
Your client is a browser and you need fallback transports (long-polling) for environments without WebSocket support
You need a fully managed real-time service with presence, pub/sub channels, and authentication built in — use Pusher, Ably, or Supabase Realtime
You want a collaborative editing or CRDT framework — use Yjs or Liveblocks instead
You need isomorphic client code that runs in both Node.js and the browser without a wrapper — ws does not work in browsers
